overview.text: Today's key developments highlight critical shifts across evaluation, infrastructure, developer tooling, and applied research in artificial intelligence. First, discussions on perplexity as a measure of progress offer developers a shared approach to evaluating emerging capabilities. Second, energy projections indicate that the vast majority of Anthropic's power will come from gas and a smaller portion from coal in the coming years. Third, new software tooling emerges, including Muru, an AI-assisted Rust server for Python applications created by mod_WSGI's author, alongside projects like fast-anything that let coding agents optimize slow functions in Python, Node, or Ruby. Fourth, notable announcements touch on mathematical milestones regarding the Riemann Hypothesis. Finally, open-source releases continue to expand practical capabilities, featuring audio-to-audio models like higurashi-ai/Haru-4B and multi-device testing frameworks such as pierridotite/mobile-agent-testers running parallel AI agents on simulators and emulators.

entries.title: EL4CTEO/fast-anything
